disclaimer: Reference data for simulation, NOT a legal determination. Before any real flight the pilot must check B4UFLY/LAANC, NOTAMs and TFRs, and get permission from the park.

frame.formula: e = (lon - datum_lon) * m_per_deg_lon; n = (lat - datum_lat) * m_per_deg_lat (env_baylands.gd geo_to_sim); Godot = (e, y, -n)
frame.heights: metres above NAVD88 (the lidar's datum). Aviation 'MSL' altitudes are taken as NAVD88 heights here; local tidal mean sea level is ~1 m above NAVD88.

rules_general.note: 14 CFR 107.51: at most 400 ft AGL (or within 400 ft of a structure). Controlled airspace (Class B, C, D, surface E) needs an FAA authorization: LAANC up to the UAS Facility Map ceiling, or FAA DroneZone. Recreational flyers (49 USC 44809) also need LAANC in controlled airspace and must pass TRUST.

park.name: Sunnyvale Baylands Park
park.note: OSM's park polygon covers the developed parkland (the city says 'over 70 acres'); the 105-acre seasonal wetlands preserve is a separate polygon (preserve).
park.manager: City of Sunnyvale (manages and maintains the park)

hours.text: The park gate is open every day from 8:00 a.m. to one half hour after sunset.

rules.rule: No balloons and no kites in the park
No pets; no dogs even on leash
Do not enter any areas posted as closed
Motorized vehicles only on designated roads and parking lots
Exclusive use of facilities by permit only

park.drone_note: No designated drone or model-aircraft area was found for this park (city Baylands page, park site map, Park Use Rules). Kites and balloons are banned to protect wildlife; expect a drone launch to need the City's permission.

preserve.name: Baylands Park seasonal wetlands preserve
preserve.note: The city says 105 acres of seasonal wetlands are protected as a wetlands preserve. No official boundary is published; this is OSM's marsh polygon east of the park (the 'Seasonal Wetlands' and salt marsh harvest mouse habitat on the city's site map), smaller than 105 acres. Treat it as a no-launch, no-low-overflight area.

uasfm.note: UAS Facility Map: the maximum altitude, ft AGL, at which the FAA may authorize Part 107 flight in each 30-arc-second cell of controlled airspace. 0 = no automatic authorization. It is NOT permission: authorization (LAANC or FAA DroneZone) is still needed. 'laanc' is derived conservatively: true only if every facility listed for the cell is LAANC-enabled; Moffett (NUQ) is not, so its cells need DroneZone.

dof_note: FAA Digital Obstacle File points (obstacles filed with the FAA). AGL/AMSL in feet as published and metres. Accuracy codes: horizontal 1 = +/-20 ft ... 4 = +/-250 ft; vertical A = +/-3 ft ... D = +/-50 ft. The lidar-built scene is the better geometry; these are a cross-check.

wind_climatology.station: NUQ (Moffett Federal Airfield ASOS), ~6 km west of the park; open bay-shore exposure like the park's
wind_climatology.time: local clock time, America/Los_Angeles (PST/PDT), hour the observation ends
wind_climatology.calm_rule: speed < 0.5 kt counts as calm (and as 0 kt in the means)
wind_climatology.direction: the direction the wind blows FROM, degrees true; 'from_deg' = vector-mean direction
wind_climatology.note: Afternoon sea breeze from the NNW-N, strongest in summer; mornings are often calm. Use it to draw training wind (speed from the month-hour distribution, direction from from_deg +/- spread); the park itself is ~6 km from NUQ and can differ.

pads_note: Chosen from the 2020 lidar (0.5 m grids): ground within a 6 m radius sloping < 3 % and rough < 0.12 m; no tree/shrub > 1.5 m, building, pole/post/fence > 1 m or water within 15 m (clear_m); >= 30 m from water; not in a closed depression deeper than 0.15 m (basin_depth_m: the park's seasonal ponds are dry in the April lidar); >= 12 m from OSM paths (path_m), >= 30 m from roads and parking (road_m), >= 60 m from power lines and towers (power_line_m); >= 10 m inside the park polygon and >= 30 m outside the wetlands preserve; >= 60 m apart; green turf (NDVI from the May 2024 NAIP photo) preferred. ground_m = metres above NAVD88. obstacle_angle_deg: steepest lidar surface seen from 2 m above the pad out to 250 m, per direction. Check the pad on the day: the lidar is from April 2020.
